outcome: Umbilical arterial (UmA) and venous (UmV) blood concentrations of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1)
cohort: Term neonates divided into three groups: uncomplicated cesarean delivery without labor (n=15), uncomplicated vaginal delivery with labor (n=15), and perinatal hypoxia-asphyxia+NE (n=8).
finding: UmA GFAP levels are elevated in neonates with hypoxia-asphyxia+NE and are modulated by placental clearance, making GFAP a more sensitive biomarker for this condition than UCH-L1.
mod_finding: UmA GFAP concentrations were lower in neonates born by cesarean delivery without labor compared to those born vaginally with labor.
